literal.prompt: Как долго на географическом Северном полюсе продолжается непрерывная ночь?

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: PASS: NOAA PMEL FAQ full question2L123-L125,exactL124,explicitly states night continuously for half year and day continuously for half year at North Pole. About half-year is appropriate astronomical/polar-night approximation,not an exact fixed number of24hour days or six calendar months. It describes continuous night/day solar visibility regime,not six months of absolute darkness without twilight. A day,a month or a whole year cannot be that half-year night phase; unique key1.

sourcesLocators.locator: Complete FAQ question2L123-L125,with ordinary/polar contextL114-L145; coreL124

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Это около полугода: на географическом Северном полюсе ночь длится непрерывно примерно половину года. В другую половину года там так же долго продолжается непрерывный день.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: PASS: exact NOAA L124 directly supports both approximately half-year night and other continuous day half-year. Current explanation keeps около/примерно,does not claim exactly equal days or no twilight. It concerns geographical North Pole,not all Arctic settlements or magnetic pole.

sourcesLocators.locator: Complete FAQ question2L123-L125,with ordinary/polar contextL114-L145; coreL124

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Сутки соответствуют обычной смене дня и ночи при вращении Земли; у Северного полюса ночная фаза длится непрерывно около половины года.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: PASS: NOAA L124 explicitly links ordinary day/night alternation to Earth spinning,then contrasts North Pole half-year night/day. Current суток note makes same ordinary-rotation vs polar-night comparison; no false claim24hours of night at pole or sidereal-rotation exact period.

sourcesLocators.locator: L123-L125: spinning Earth ordinary day/night and polar contrast

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: В другую половину года на Северном полюсе непрерывно длится день: Солнце остаётся над горизонтом.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: PASS: NOAA L124 explicitly says day continuously for half year as counterpart. Current correct note adds that other season has continuous daylight/Sun above horizon,not just repeating night duration/key. Knowing long winter night alone would not specify whether remaining season has ordinary daily alternation or continuous daylight at that location; this is useful extra solar-regime fact.

sourcesLocators.locator: L124: continuous day counterpart for half year

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Синодический месяц — промежуток между новолуниями; его средняя длина составляет около 29,5 суток.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: PASS: full original USNO glossaryL384 distinguishes general/calendrical month,L386 sidereal27.322days,andL387 explicitly defines synodic month between successive new moons with mean29.531days. Current note names synodic type and rounds mean to about29.5; not a claim every calendar month is29.5days or confusion with27.3day sidereal period.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: За год у полюса проходят обе непрерывные фазы: примерно полгода ночи и полгода дня.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: PASS: NOAA L124 gives both approximately half-year continuous phases; their annual cycle is one year. Current year note relates year alternative to full cycle containing both night and day,not entire year of uninterrupted darkness. It is an affirmative useful comparison,not a negative placeholder.
